In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the efficacy of ICaL blockade as a strategy for AF termination is highly variable, depending on the underlying sodium channel availability.
a combination of ICaL and INa blockade may be the best approach to terminate AF, especially in patients with a depressed basal INa availability.
the balance between sodium and calcium channels is a key determinant in the effectiveness of antiarrhythic drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the balance between sodium and calcium channels is a critical factor in the efficacy of calcium channel blockers in the treatment of AF.
the efficacy of ICaL blockade as an antiarrhythmia strategy depends on the basal availability and expression of sodium and calcium currents.
the balance between INa and ICal is critical for AF termination and that the efficacy of ICal block is dependent on the underlying expression of INa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a population of mathematical models with realistic intersubjective variability can be used to identify the underlying mechanisms that maintain atrial fibrillation.
the efficacy of a given pharmacological intervention can be predicted by the baseline expression of sodium and calcium channels.
the efficacy of ICaL blockers is highly dependent on the underlying expression levels of the other ion channels, particularly INa.
